# OpenCode TTS

[![Works with OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/brand/badges/opencode-works-with-a-light-20.svg)](https://opencode.ai)

Text-to-speech for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) replies on Windows.

A small C++ helper uses Windows SAPI voices, and a local OpenCode plugin speaks
the final assistant reply after each turn. It listens for
`session.execution.succeeded`, cleans Markdown from the reply, and speaks the
most recent assistant message that contains text.

## Install as an OpenCode plugin

The repo includes a local plugin at `release/plugin/index.ts` and a portable
config template at `release/config.snippet.jsonc`. After copying `release` into
your project, the config should contain:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    "-opencode.tts",
    {
      "package": "./.opencode/plugins/tts",
      "options": {
        "enabled": true,
        "exe": "release\\tts.exe",
        "voice": "Zira",
        "rate": 1,
        "volume": 100,
        "maxChars": 1200,
        "mode": "interrupt",
        "debug": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Run `.\release\install.ps1` from the project root to install the plugin and write
this config for you, then reload OpenCode with
`opencode api post /api/location/reload`.

## Quick start

1. Copy the `release` folder into your OpenCode project, or clone this repo and
   run OpenCode from the repo root.
2. Run the installer from the project root:

   ```powershell
   .\release\install.ps1
   ```

3. Ask OpenCode something:

   ```powershell
   opencode run "Reply with exactly: OpenCode TTS is working"
   ```

You should hear the reply in the default voice (**Zira**). See
[`release/README.md`](release/README.md) for the full option list and
troubleshooting.

## Natural voices (optional)

The built-in SAPI voices (David, Zira) work offline but sound dated. For a more
natural voice on Windows 11:

1. Install a Narrator natural voice under
   **Settings → Accessibility → Narrator → Narrator's voice → Add natural
   voices** (Aria, Jenny, or Guy).
2. Install [NaturalVoiceSAPIAdapter](https://github.com/gexgd0419/NaturalVoiceSAPIAdapter)
   to expose those voices to SAPI applications. It is a separate MIT-licensed
   project and is not bundled here.
3. Set `"voice": "Aria"` in `opencode.jsonc`, then reload:

   ```powershell
   opencode api post /api/location/reload
   ```

Check available voices with:

```powershell
.\release\tts.exe --list-voices
```

## Contents

- `release/tts.exe` — release speaker (MSVC `/O2 /MT`, statically linked runtime)
- `release/plugin/index.ts` — OpenCode plugin source
- `release/install.ps1` — installs the plugin and writes `opencode.jsonc`
- `release/config.snippet.jsonc` — portable starter config
- `OpenCodeTTS/` — C++ source and Visual Studio project

## Building from source

Open `OpenCodeTTS\OpenCodeTTS.sln` in Visual Studio and build `Release|x64`, or
run:

```powershell
cmd /c OpenCodeTTS\build-release.bat
```

The build scripts locate Visual Studio with `vswhere.exe`.

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 with SAPI voices
- OpenCode with local plugin support
- No cloud service or API key is required

# OpenCode TTS — source and development

Release package is in `..\release\`. Start there if you just want to try it.

## Source files

- `tts.cpp` — C++ helper source (v1.0.0)
- `tts.exe` — development build
- `build.bat` — development build
- `build-release.bat` — builds `..\release\tts.exe`
- `OpenCodeTTS.sln` / `OpenCodeTTS.vcxproj` — Visual Studio project
- `..\.opencode\plugins\tts\index.ts` — installed plugin
- `..\opencode.jsonc` — plugin configuration

## Speaker features

- Windows SAPI voices (David and Zira on this machine)
- Text from arguments, `--stdin`, or `--file`
- Voice selection by exact or partial name
- Rate/volume control
- `--list-voices`, `--check`, `--version`
- Optional `--log` file

## Build

```powershell
cmd /c build.bat
cmd /c build-release.bat
```

Or open `OpenCodeTTS.sln` in Visual Studio and build `Release|x64`.

## Plugin

The plugin listens for `session.execution.succeeded`, reads the last assistant
text message, cleans Markdown/code blocks, and speaks it through the release
speaker.

Options in `..\opencode.jsonc`:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Turn speech on/off |
| `exe` | `release\tts.exe` | Speaker path |
| `voice` | `Zira` | Voice name |
| `rate` | `1` | -10 to 10 |
| `volume` | `100` | 0 to 100 |
| `maxChars` | `1200` | Reply truncation |
| `mode` | `interrupt` | `interrupt` or `queue` |
| `debug` | `false` | Log spoken text |

Reload after edits:

```powershell
opencode api post /api/location/reload
```

## Notes

- Speech is local/offline.
- It speaks on this Windows PC, not on a remote Raspberry Pi.
- To speak on another machine, point `exe` at a wrapper that sends text to that
  machine's TTS service.

# OpenCode TTS — Release 1.0.0

Text-to-speech for OpenCode replies. The C++ helper uses Windows SAPI voices,
so it speaks on this Windows PC. A local OpenCode plugin speaks the final
assistant reply after each turn.

## Try it

1. Run `install.ps1` in this folder.
2. Ask OpenCode anything, for example:
   ```powershell
   opencode run "Reply with exactly: OpenCode TTS release is working"
   ```
3. You should hear the reply spoken with the Microsoft Zira voice.

## Contents

- `tts.exe` — release speaker, built with MSVC `/O2 /MT`
- `plugin/index.ts` — OpenCode plugin source
- `config.snippet.jsonc` — exact config used by this release
- `install.ps1` — installs plugin and config
- `VERSION` — release version

## Speaker options

```powershell
.\tts.exe --check
.\tts.exe --list-voices
.\tts.exe "Hello"
.\tts.exe --voice David --rate 0 --volume 80 "Slightly slower"
.\tts.exe --file reply.txt --log C:\temp\tts.log
type reply.txt | .\tts.exe --stdin
```

## Plugin options

Edit `opencode.jsonc` in the project root:

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Turn speech on/off |
| `exe` | `release\tts.exe` | Path to speaker |
| `voice` | `Zira` | Exact or partial voice name |
| `rate` | `1` | -10 to 10 |
| `volume` | `100` | 0 to 100 |
| `maxChars` | `1200` | Reply truncation limit |
| `mode` | `interrupt` | `interrupt` or `queue` |
| `debug` | `false` | Write spoken text to `release\tts-invocations.log` |

Environment overrides also work: `OPENCODE_TTS_ENABLED`, `OPENCODE_TTS_EXE`,
`OPENCODE_TTS_VOICE`, `OPENCODE_TTS_RATE`, `OPENCODE_TTS_VOLUME`,
`OPENCODE_TTS_MAX_CHARS`, `OPENCODE_TTS_MODE`, `OPENCODE_TTS_DEBUG`.

## Troubleshooting

- Confirm plugin is active: `opencode plugin list`
- Confirm speaker is healthy: `.\tts.exe --check`
- Reload after config edits: `opencode api post /api/location/reload`
- If no sound, check Windows volume and the default output device.

## Source

Buildable Visual Studio project and development scripts live in
`..\OpenCodeTTS\`.
